Yarra River Water Quality (Cleaned Dataset)

yarra_river_data.Rd

A processed water-quality dataset for analyzing environmental trends in the Yarra River. The data is suitable for visualization, exploratory data analysis, statistical modelling, and interactive applications. The dataset is provided in a wide format, where each row represents a single observation at a monitoring site and each column corresponds to a measured water-quality variable.

Usage

yarra_river_data

Format

A data frame with N rows and 7 variables:

site_id

Character. Monitoring site identifier.

datetime

POSIXct. Timestamp of the observation (local time).

ph

Numeric. Acidity/alkalinity of water (0–14 scale).

salinity_ec25

Numeric. Electrical conductivity at 25°C (\(\mu\)S/cm), used as a proxy for salinity.

turbidity

Numeric. Turbidity (NTU), higher values indicate murkier water.

nitrogen_total

Numeric. Total nitrogen concentration (mg/L), a key nutrient linked to algal growth.

water_temperature

Numeric. Water temperature (°C), affects dissolved oxygen and species tolerance.

Source

Yarra River monitoring dataset provided for ETC5523 (Monash University).

Details

The cleaning and reshaping steps are fully reproducible and recorded in data-raw/yarra_river_data.R. The original raw Excel file is also stored in data-raw/.

This dataset was created via the script data-raw/yarra_river_data.R using readxl, dplyr, and tidyr. Variables were cleaned, filtered to key water-quality indicators, and reshaped to wide format using tidyr::pivot_wider().

See also

run_app for an optional interactive visualisation, or simply load the data with data("yarra_river_data").

Examples

data("yarra_river_data", package = "yarraclean")
str(yarra_river_data)
#> tibble [225 × 7] (S3: tbl_df/tbl/data.frame)
#>  $ site_id          : num [1:225] 229143 229143 229143 229143 229143 ...
#>  $ datetime         : POSIXct[1:225], format: "1991-01-08 13:50:00" "1991-02-12 09:35:00" ...
#>  $ nitrogen_total   : num [1:225] NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA ...
#>  $ ph               : num [1:225] 7.1 7 6.2 6.7 7.7 6.9 6.1 6.7 0 7.7 ...
#>  $ salinity_ec25    : num [1:225] 230 370 390 160 200 160 250 0 170 150 ...
#>  $ turbidity        : num [1:225] 35 36 18 20 17 79 0 41 45 17 ...
#>  $ water_temperature: num [1:225] 21 21.4 22.2 16.8 17.5 12.2 11 10.2 12 16 ...
